problem:
Let
$E=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}]$
and
$F=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ Then, the dimensions of $EF$ are{{field-1}}$\times $
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
We notice that $E$ is a $3\times 2$ matrix and $F$ is a $2\times 1$ matrix. 

There are $2$ columns in $E$ and $2$ rows in $F.$ Since the number of columns in $E$ equals the number of rows in $F,$ the matrices $E$ and $F$ are conformable for multiplication. 

The product $EF$ has dimensions $3\times 1:$ 

$$
{E}_{3\times \boxed{\text{2}}}{\times }_{✓}{F}_{\boxed{\text{2}}\times 1}={EF}_{3\times 1}
$$
